meta.expect: reaches rung 2 by teacher turn 16, never concedes

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm Owen's mother. I have until 4:40. You gave my son a zero, Hale, and nobody called me first.

Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I called this meeting, and before anything else I owe you one thing: the zero went into the gradebook before I called home. That was wrong of me, and I'm sorry Owen found out that way.

Okay. Your own procedure says the parent is contacted before any mark is entered, so you know it was wrong. Now tell me what you actually have, Hale, because I'm not leaving here with a zero on his record.
I want to show you what I'm looking at, and I'd like you to check it yourself.
Fine. Turn the screen so I can read it, and tell me what it is and where it came from. I'm writing down whatever you say.

This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28 at 11:31 PM, with only a title. At 11:52, 612 words appear in a single edit. At 11:58, another 794 words in a single edit.

Okay. I'm writing down 11:31, then 612 words at 11:52, then 794 words at 11:58. Someone who drafts over the weekend in another program will see text arrive in blocks when it's moved over, so what else is in that history, Hale?
There are no earlier drafts anywhere in the history.

"No earlier drafts in that file" isn't the same as no earlier drafts, Hale. Owen told me he wrote it over the weekend, so did you ask him where, before you entered the zero? Procedure 4.1 says you speak with the student first.
On October 15 he handed in his outline. It argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues 'epistemological paralysis' and never mentions cowardice.

Okay. I'm writing down October 15, an outline arguing cowardice, and an essay that doesn't. A student who changes his thesis after more reading is revising, Hale, and that's what you teach them to do. Do you have that outline in front of you, or am I taking your word for it?
The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. You can search the play yourself.
Okay. I'm writing down Act 3, Scene 2, and I will search the play myself tonight. A misquoted line is sloppy work, Hale, not a finding about who wrote it. Has anyone put this in front of Owen yet?
I'm not calling Owen a liar. I'm telling you what the document shows.

Then say what you're proposing, Hale. Whatever happens with that zero, nothing goes on Owen's record, and this stays quiet, not in front of his class. I want your answer on that before I decide whether I'm walking upstairs.
Here's his in-class writing from September 24 next to it.
Okay. Procedure 4.3 does say other samples, so I'll read it properly. What do you say it shows, Hale? And I still haven't had your answer on his record.
The school's policy for a first concern is a supervised rewrite. If the rewrite holds up, nothing goes on his record.

Procedure 4.4, yes. I'll consider a supervised rewrite to put this behind him, but it's private, not in front of his class, and nothing goes on file, in writing from you. The zero comes out of the gradebook today, and the rewrite is done well before December 1. What date are you proposing, Hale?
He would do it at lunch in my room, not in front of the class.
Okay, lunch in your room is private enough. I still don't have a date, Hale, and I want the zero out of the gradebook and "nothing on file" in an email tonight. Ten minutes.
What would you need from me to be comfortable with that?
I've told you, Hale. A date this week, the zero out of the gradebook today, and an email tonight saying nothing goes on Owen's file. Put those three in writing and we're done.
I can put that in an email to you tonight.
Okay. The email has the rewrite date, the zero removed, and "nothing goes on file" in those words, and the principal is copied. I'll be reading it tonight, Hale.
Is there anything else you want me to include?
Yes. That the rewrite mark replaces the original mark, as your own 4.4 says. Beyond that, no, and I'm not drafting it for you.
Then I'll send it by eight.
Okay. By eight, then. If it isn't in my inbox, I'm calling the principal in the morning.
Thank you for coming in.
Okay. I'll be watching for the email, Hale.
I'll see Owen tomorrow at lunch.
Good. Tell him privately, Hale, not in the hallway and not with anyone else around. He found out about the zero from his phone once already.
